alreadyFollowing.description: Whether the viewer already follows this follower back.

handle.description: The follower's public handle — addresses /u/[handle] + the follow toggle.

ActivityIconKind.description: Which glyph a row renders. ⚠️ `remix` and `featured` are planned, not live: no NotificationEventKey produces them today (see ACTIVITY_FEED_EVENT_KEYS above), so no builder below emits them. They are part of the published wire contract, so a client should tolerate them rather than assume a closed set — but nothing will render them until the events ship.

availabilityVersion.description: Client-visible freshness token for the exact request context. Exact slots are reusable only when this matches.

generatedAt.description: ISO timestamp for when the payload was generated.

professionalId.description: Transitional duplicate fields. Prefer `request.*` in all new code.

selectedDay.description: Canonical enterprise field. Authoritative for first paint because it belongs to the current bootstrap response.

AuthSessionHandoffResponseDTO.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/session-handoff

One-time sign-in hand-off for a native client opening a web page. The response carries the ABSOLUTE exchange URL rather than the bare token, so the client never assembles an auth URL itself (and so the exchange path can move without an app release). Opening `url` in a browser consumes the token, sets the normal session cookie and redirects to `redirectPath`.

`url` is single-use and expires at `expiresAt` (ISO-8601, ≤60s out) — treat it as a credential: open it immediately, never persist or log it.

AvailabilityLocationOption.description: One bookable salon/suite option for the primary pro. Present so the client can choose which location to visit when the pro has several. Empty for mobile mode.

offeringId.description: Optional on the generic UI card because primary vs alternate cards have slightly different guarantees. Use the specialized types below when availability context must guarantee bookability.

slots.description: UI convenience only. Do not treat these as globally authoritative without request/version validation.

offeringId.description: Optional on the generic UI card because primary vs alternate cards have slightly different guarantees. Use the specialized types below when availability context must guarantee bookability.

BookingBeforeAfterThumbs.description:
The primary "before" and "after" photo for a booking, already resolved to renderable URLs (signed for the private session bucket, public otherwise).

This is the single source of truth for the before/after pair shown anywhere that links to a client's aftercare summary (home action card, aftercare inbox, …) — so those surfaces don't each re-implement the media select + phase pick + URL rendering.

durationMinutes.description: Minutes actually RESERVED — base service + any `addOnIds` sent with the create — excluding the location's buffer. Finalize enforces the same arithmetic, so this is what the slot is being held for (B1-A).

CalendarSwatchId.description:
The twelve calendar swatch ids (K7). A pro picks one of these per service offering (K8); the calendar paints it on the event card's accent stripe.

🔴 A FIXED set, deliberately — never a free hex picker. A raw colour skips `[data-mode]` (a hue that reads on paper vanishes on ink), skips the contrast budget, and is not caught by any static guard. Twelve tokens with a tuned light/dark pair each is the only version that survives white-label.

🔴 A DEDICATED palette, not the brand hues — every one of those is semantically loaded (`colorAmber` *is* `--tone-pending`, `colorEmber` *is* `--tone-danger`, `colorFern` *is* `--tone-success`), so a service coloured amber would read as "pending".

ChannelPreferenceState.description:
Read/write surface for the *NotificationPreference tables. The delivery engine already consumes these rows (see channelPolicy.ts); this module only lets a user view and edit their own rows. It changes no policy default.

Quiet hours are stored per-eventKey on every preference row, so a single user-facing window is written uniformly across all of an owner's rows.

To tell "never configured" apart from "explicitly turned off", we use a sentinel the engine already treats as no-quiet-hours: equal start/end minutes (channelPolicy.isWithinQuietHours returns false when start === end). So:   - both null               → never configured → UI default ON (22:00–08:00)   - start === end (e.g. 0)  → explicitly OFF   - start !== end           → explicitly ON with that window

CheckoutStripeSessionOrSettledDTO.description: The final bill's session, which — unlike the deposit's — may legitimately not exist: when a paid deposit covers the whole total there is nothing to charge and no session is created. Kept separate from `StripeCheckoutSessionDTO` so the deposit route's non-null contract is not weakened for every consumer.

depositCreditCents.description: Deposit money credited against this bill, in cents. On the charge branch this is what was subtracted from the total to get the amount charged; 0 when no deposit applies.

settledByDeposit.description: The deposit covered the entire bill: checkout is already PAID, no session was created, and the client owes nothing. `stripeCheckout.url` is null on this branch — a client that only reads the url still behaves correctly (it has nowhere to send them) rather than charging a stale amount.

professionalName.description: Pro's public display name (respects nameDisplay); never null.

scheduledFor.description: ISO-8601 instant, or null when the booking has no scheduled time.

timeZone.description: IANA timezone the appointment should be rendered in; clients format it.

booking.description: Booking context, or null for a booking-less claim.

invitedName.description: The name/contact the pro put on file for this claim (invite snapshot).

professionalName.description: Pro's public display name resolved from the booking OR the invite's own pro (respects nameDisplay); null for a pro-less claim (cold self-serve orphan).

markReadEventKeys.description: The event keys "Mark all read" should clear (the activity allowlist).

unreadCount.description: Unread activity events — the same count that badges the Me header bell.

followBack.description: Present for a follow item whose follower is publicly addressable.

href.description: Where the row (and any "View" CTA) links, when applicable.

timestamp.description: ISO timestamp; the client formats it relative.

radiusMiles.description: SEARCH_AREA only: the discovery search radius in miles (5–50), the cross-device-synced counterpart of the local viewer radius. Null for a SERVICE_ADDRESS or a search area saved before a radius was set.

ClientAftercareCheckoutProductDTO.description: The client's current booking-checkout product selection — one line per recommendation they've added, with the snapshotted unit price. Mirrors `BookingCheckoutProductItem`.

unitPrice.description: Decimal-string unit price snapshot (per the wire money convention).

aftercare.description: The sent aftercare summary (care notes), or null when none is sent yet.

beforeAfter.description: Primary before/after pair (featured, else earliest per phase).

canShowAftercare.description: Whether the client's aftercare surface is visible for this booking — mirrors the web `canShowAftercareTab` gate (booking COMPLETED, or a sent aftercare summary exists). When false the native client hides the section.

checkoutProducts.description: The client's current booking-checkout product selection (empty if none).

checkoutProductsEditable.description: Whether the client may edit their checkout-product selection right now — mirrors the write path's `assertClientCanEditBookingCheckoutProducts` gate (finalized aftercare, not yet in/through payment, not completed/cancelled). When false the native + web pickers render read-only.

existingReview.description: The client's existing review for this booking (text only), or null when they haven't left one yet / no summary is sent. Prefills the native review block for editing. Gated like `aftercare`.

rebook.description: The pro's rebook recommendation (recommended window / proposed next appointment) + the coupled next booking, or null when no summary is sent.

recommendedProducts.description: The pro's product recommendations from the sent summary (empty if none).

reviewEligible.description: Whether the client may leave or edit a review right now — mirrors the write path's `canBookingAcceptClientReview` closeout gate (completed + finished booking, finalized aftercare, collected payment). False until a summary is sent. When false the native review block stays hidden.

ClientAftercareExistingReviewDTO.description: The client's own review of this booking, when they've left one. Mirrors the web `SafeExistingReview` (text slice + attached media); powers prefill + edit and the photo grid in the native review block. Gated like `aftercare` (only surfaced once a summary is sent).

body.description: Optional free-text review body, or null.

mediaAssets.description: Photos/videos the client attached to their review (newest first; empty when none). The client can add more (fresh uploads or "from this session") or remove one (DELETE /client/reviews/[id]/media/[mediaId]).

rating.description: The 1–5 star rating the client gave.

aftercareId.description: The AftercareSummary id, when present on the notification.

beforeAfter.description: The pro-chosen (or earliest) before/after pair, or null when none.

body.description: The notification body copy the pro wrote, or null.

bookingId.description: The visit this aftercare belongs to; null if the notification lost its link.

createdAt.description: When the aftercare landed in the inbox (ISO).

notificationId.description: The AFTERCARE_READY notification id (stable list key).

proId.description: The pro's profile id for a profile deep-link, or null.

proName.description: The pro's public display name (honors nameDisplay), or "Your pro".

rebookMode.description: The aftercare rebook mode, driving the row hint; null when unset.

rebookedFor.description: The pro's recommended rebook date (ISO), when set.

timeZone.description: The booking's sanitized IANA timezone for rendering `scheduledFor`.

title.description: Canonical booking title (service + add-ons), or a fallback.

unread.description: True while the client hasn't opened this aftercare (drives the NEW pill).

ClientAftercareNextBookingDTO.description: The AFTERCARE-sourced next booking coupled to this booking (its `rebookOfBookingId` points back here). Lets the aftercare rebook card show a confirmed / pending-approval state instead of re-offering Confirm. Mirrors the web `rebookedNextBooking` load.

scheduledFor.description: Scheduled instant (ISO), or null when unset.

status.description: The next booking's lifecycle status (PENDING until the pro approves, etc.).

ClientAftercareRebookDTO.description: The pro's rebook recommendation from the sent aftercare summary + the coupled next booking (if the client has already rebooked). Mirrors the web page's `getAftercareRebookInfo` inputs (`aftercareSummarySelect` rebook fields) plus the `rebookedNextBooking` load — powers the native rebook-window card. Present only when a summary has been sent (same gate as `aftercare`).

declinedAt.description: ISO instant the client declined the pro's proposed `BOOKED_NEXT_APPOINTMENT`, else null. Cleared when the pro re-offers.

mode.description: The pro's rebook mode: `NONE` (no recommendation), `RECOMMENDED_WINDOW` (a date range the client picks within), or `BOOKED_NEXT_APPOINTMENT` (a specific time the pro proposed for the client to confirm/decline).

nextBooking.description: The coupled AFTERCARE-sourced next booking when one exists (the client has confirmed/booked), else null.

rebookedFor.description: The pro-proposed next-appointment instant for `BOOKED_NEXT_APPOINTMENT` (ISO), else null. Not set for `RECOMMENDED_WINDOW`.

ClientAftercareRecommendedProductDTO.description: One product the pro recommended in the aftercare summary. Internal recommendations (`productId` + `product` set) can be added to the booking checkout; external ones (`externalName`/`externalUrl`) are link-outs only. Mirrors the web `AftercareProductRecommendationsCard` recommendation shape.

externalName.description: Display name for an external (link-out) recommendation, else null.

externalUrl.description: Link target for an external recommendation, else null.

note.description: Optional free-text note the pro attached to the recommendation.

retailPrice.description: Decimal-string retail price (per the wire money convention), or null.

product.description: The internal product (name/brand/price), or null for external recs.

productId.description: The internal Product id when this is an in-app recommendation, else null.

ClientAftercareReviewMediaDTO.description: One photo/video attached to the client's review, with render-ready URLs. Review media lives in the public bucket (visibility PUBLIC — attaching to a review is the publish-consent action); the URLs are resolved the same way the web booking-detail page resolves the review's `mediaAssets`. Powers the native review photo grid (A3-rev 4b).

createdAt.description: ISO instant the media was attached to the review.

url.description: Render-ready full-size URL, or null when it can't be resolved.

ClientAftercareSummaryDTO.description: The care-notes slice of a SENT aftercare summary the client may read.

notes.description: Free-text care instructions the pro wrote for the client.

sentToClientAt.description: ISO instant the pro sent this aftercare to the client.

depositAmount.description: Decimal deposit amount string (e.g. "25.00"), formatted client-side like the other checkout amounts. Null when no deposit applies.

depositDisputed.description: The discovery deposit charge is under (or lost) a Stripe dispute.

depositStatus.description: Discovery deposit lifecycle (BookingDepositStatus): NONE · PENDING · PAID · REFUNDED · FAILED. A deposit is OWED-and-unpaid exactly when this is "PENDING" — that's the gate for a "Pay deposit" CTA. Populated only where the source query selects the deposit columns (the client bookings list route); null elsewhere.

paymentDisputed.description: Final-bill refund/dispute truth, so a card can't keep showing a plain "paid" after the money moved back or the charge was disputed (M11 display-truth). Computed server-side. `paymentCollectedAt`/`checkoutStatus` are monotonic and never reverse on a refund/dispute — these do. Populated only where the source query selects the stripe/dispute columns (the client bookings list route + the booking-detail loader); default (false / 0) elsewhere.

paymentFullyRefunded.description: The whole captured final bill has been refunded — money is back with the client.

paymentRefundedCents.description: Cumulative cents refunded against the final-bill charge (0 when none).

cancellationPolicy.description: The no-show / late-cancel fee policy the client AGREED to at booking (M15), formatted for display, or null if none applied. Sourced from the booking's own `cancellationPolicySnapshot` (what they agreed to — never the pro's possibly-since-edited live settings), so the detail always shows the honest, agreed terms. Populated only where the source query selects the snapshot.

clientConfirmation.description: K11's client-confirmation state, derived by the one helper (lib/booking/clientConfirmation.ts) and rendered VERBATIM — the client app never recomputes it. OPTIONAL and absent unless the pro's reminder actually asked: with the loop flag off (prod today) every booking reads NOT_REQUESTED, so this key never appears and the payload is byte-identical to pre-K13. Its presence is the app's cue to offer the in-app answer (POST /api/v1/client/bookings/[id]/confirmation { answer }) — which is why it is suppressed outright while ENABLE_CLIENT_CONFIRMATION_LOOP is off, even for a row that carries stamps from an earlier trial: that route refuses, and a control the server will reject must not be drawn.

hasPendingRebookConfirmation.description: True when the pro proposed a next appointment (aftercare BOOKED_NEXT_APPOINTMENT) the client hasn't confirmed or declined yet — drives the rebook-confirm CTA. Confirm/decline via POST /api/v1/client/bookings/[id]/aftercare-rebook { action }. Populated only where the source query selects the aftercare/rebook columns (the client bookings list route and the /me page loader); false elsewhere.

mediaUseConsent.description: True when the client has granted the pro media-use consent for this session (allow featuring their photos/video publicly — portfolio/Looks). Toggle via POST /api/v1/client/bookings/[id]/media-consent { granted }. Populated only where the source query selects `mediaUseConsentAt` (the client bookings list route); false elsewhere.

paymentOptions.description: The pro's accepted payment methods (with off-platform handles) + tip config + payment note for this booking's checkout. Populated only where the caller loads the pro's payment settings (the client bookings list route, for the native checkout); null elsewhere. Handles are gated to the client's own booking — never exposed on public surfaces.

rebookOfBookingId.description: When this booking is a rebook, the id of the appointment it was booked off of (the `RebookChain` source). For an aftercare-sourced PENDING rebook whose source payment is AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, this links the two so the native next-booking detail can label it "pending — your pro will confirm after payment". Null for a standalone booking. Populated only where the source query selects `rebookOfBookingId` (the client bookings list route).

rebookProposedFor.description: The pro-proposed next-appointment instant (ISO) when one is pending; else null.

collectPaymentAt.description: "AT_BOOKING" | "AFTER_SERVICE" (or null when the pro has no settings row).

tipSuggestions.description: Whole-percent tip presets on the services subtotal; the client prepends 0%.

description.description: Plain-words expansion for tooltips and accessibility labels — the calendar card renders this state as a GLYPH (K7's corner channel), and a screen reader must get the words, never a shape (K5's rule).

label.description: The short display words ("Client confirmed") — what a pill prints.

significant.description: false only for NOT_REQUESTED: a booking nobody asked a confirmation for renders NOTHING anywhere — absence is the honest display, and as of K11 (no writers yet) that is every booking, which is exactly the ship-dark default. The DECISION lives here so surfaces can't drift on it.

publicIncentive.description:
The incentive THIS client was matched on, already reduced to display copy ("20% off", "$40 off", "Free service") — the same block the openings feed sends, built by the same `pickRecipientTierPlan` + `mapPublicIncentiveDto` helpers so the two surfaces cannot word the same offer differently.

The raw `tierPlans` above are every tier's plan and say nothing about which one applies to this recipient; picking one client-side would mean re-implementing the tier resolution AND the label. Null when the matched plan carries no incentive.

path.description: Root-relative share path (/c/{shortCode}); clients absolutize it.

lookName.description: The author's look that inspired the booking.

proName.description: The pro the remix was booked with.

who.description: Booker, PII-safe: `@handle` for a public client, else a generic label.

creator.description: Real-data creator metrics + remixes. `isCreator` gates the whole creator UI: false until the client has published at least one authored look.

availableWorkspaces.description:
Every workspace this user is entitled to act in, from the same `listAvailableWorkspaces` the web switcher gates on. Native has no other way to know: the acting role above is always CLIENT, and the session JWT carries only that acting role — so a dual-role pro browsing as a client is otherwise indistinguishable on the wire from a client-only account. That is what stranded iOS clients with no way back to the pro shell.

Always present and always contains `CLIENT` (anyone may act as a client); a length of 1 means "don't offer a switch", matching web's `buildWorkspaceOptions` returning [] for a single workspace.

role.description: The workspace the user is ACTING in — always `CLIENT` here, since this payload is gated by requireClient. Never a capability signal: see `availableWorkspaces` for that.

data.description: Structured, event-specific metadata. Non-object payloads serialize to null.

readAt.description: ISO timestamp when the client read it, or null while unread.

nextCursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, or null when the feed is exhausted.

ClientPaymentMethodConfirmRequestDTO.description: Request body for POST /api/v1/client/payment-methods (persist a confirmed card).

setupIntentId.description: The SetupIntent the client just confirmed with Stripe.js.

ClientPaymentMethodConfirmResponseDTO.description: Response for POST /api/v1/client/payment-methods (a card was persisted).

ClientPaymentMethodDTO.description: A single saved card, safe to render (never the full PAN).

brand.description: Card network, e.g. "visa" | "mastercard". Null until Stripe details load.

createdAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the card was saved.

isDefault.description: The card charged first for no-show fees. Exactly one default per client.

last4.description: Last four digits of the card. Null until Stripe details load.

clientSecret.description: SetupIntent client secret to confirm the card with Stripe.js on the client.

customerId.description: The client's Stripe Billing customer id.

publishableKey.description: The Stripe publishable key to initialize the client SDK with. Web reads this from the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` bundle inline and ignores this field; native clients (which can't inline build-time env) use it so the key always matches the backend's Stripe mode (test vs live). Empty string if unconfigured.

setupIntentId.description: SetupIntent id, echoed back to the confirm (POST payment-methods) step.

ConsentFormOption.description: The choices a pro has when recording a consent record: their ACTIVE forms, each resolved to the version that would be signed today. Retired forms are absent — a form a pro has stopped using should not keep being attached to new records, while records already pointing at it keep resolving their own version.

ConsentFormVersionAttestation.description: K14 — the form version a record attests to, resolved as it was signed. Null on every pre-K14 row (free-text records, which stay readable) and on any record a pro chose not to attach a form to.

description.description: The plain-words expansion, for tooltips and accessible names. The calendar card renders a chip, but the words are what a screen reader gets (K5's rule), and they NAME the form — "which waiver?" is the pro's next question.

label.description: What a chip prints. Kind-neutral: a patch test is not a "waiver".

significant.description:
🔴 False for a booking that is already OVER.

A pro who sets their first requirement today would otherwise light up every past appointment for that service in amber — warnings about visits that already happened, which nobody can act on. The DECISION lives here so no surface can drift on it (the K1 `significant` rule).

JsonObject.description: From https://github.com/sindresorhus/type-fest/ Matches a JSON object. This type can be useful to enforce some input to be JSON-compatible or as a super-type to be extended from.

JsonValue.description: From https://github.com/sindresorhus/type-fest/ Matches any valid JSON value.

answers.description: Creation-question chip answers (question key → chosen option value), validated against the type's question set in lib/boards/context.ts. Owner-only — never exposed on the public board page.

eventDate.description: Calendar date the board counts down to (`YYYY-MM-DD`), bridal/prom only.

slug.description: URL-safe slug for the public /u/[handle]/boards/[slug] address.

type.description: What the board is for (creation-context, personalization spec §7).

eventDate.description: Calendar date the board counts down to (`YYYY-MM-DD`), bridal/prom only.

type.description: What the board is for (creation-context, personalization spec §7).

before.description: Opt-in before/after pairing → render the comparison slider when present.

eyebrow.description: Server-computed context label for the row's eyebrow, e.g. "BOOKING CONFIRMED — Balayage — Fri 2:00 PM", "Waitlist — Position active", "Service — Color". Always present (falls back to "Message"). Computed once server-side so web + iOS render identical copy without duplicating the booking/waitlist/service lookups.

isAccentContext.description: Whether the eyebrow renders in the accent tone (actionable context).

isViewerPro.description: Whether the viewer is this thread's professional (derived from the viewer's user id, not their acting role — so dual-role users and admins never resolve to their own name). The counterparty is the client when true, the pro when false. The list payload omits participant user ids, so this is the client's only signal for picking whose name/avatar to show.

counterpartyLastReadAt.description: The counterparty's last-read timestamp (ISO-8601), or null if they haven't read the thread. Drives the sender's read receipt: an outgoing message is "Read" once this is >= the message's createdAt. Updated on each poll.

displayName.description: Server-resolved public display name honoring the pro's `nameDisplay` toggle (business name / real name /

emailLocked.description: When true, the EMAIL toggle is locked on — this is a critical event (e.g. a payment receipt) whose email can never be turned off. The engine enforces this regardless of the saved preference; the UI just reflects it.

supportedChannels.description: Channels this event can use for this audience (the only toggles shown).

group.description: Add-on grouping label (e.g. "Color"), or null when ungrouped.

id.description: OfferingAddOn link id — the value to send back in finalize's `addOnIds`.

serviceId.description: The underlying add-on service id (not what finalize wants — use `id`).

cancellationPolicy.description: The pro's no-show / late-cancel fee policy the client must agree to before booking (M15), formatted for display, or null when the pro charges no fees (or the feature flag is off). When non-null, the native confirm flow shows it and requires the agreement checkbox; acceptance is sent to finalize.

defaultAddressId.description: Default client mobile address (only resolved for an authed mobile claim).

services.description: JSON-safe (Decimal -> string) services + incentive blocks for native clients.

PairedBeforeDto.description: The chosen "before" of an opt-in before/after pair, resolved to renderable URLs. Present on a displayed asset (portfolio tile / review after-photo) that a pro or client paired; null → render the asset as a single tile. The tile's own `src`/`thumbUrl` are the "after".

label.description: Ready-to-render wording — iOS shows this string verbatim (K2 parity).

significant.description: false only for UNPAID: dense surfaces (the calendar card) skip the badge there — a wall of "Unpaid" on every upcoming appointment is noise, and absence already reads as "nothing collected". List/detail surfaces may still render it. The DECISION lives here so surfaces can't drift on it.

from.description: Echoed range, "YYYY-MM-DD" inclusive — `to` may be clamped by the server.

openSlots.description: The open-slot overlay's state. `null` when the request carried no service context at all — the classic "which days am I busy" call.

tz.description: The IANA zone the day buckets were computed in.

publicProfileHandle.description:
The client's public `@handle`, or null when they have no public profile.

This is NOT the same axis as `canViewClient`, and the two are deliberately independent: `canViewClient` says whether this pro may open the private CHART, while this says whether the client has a world-readable page at `/u/{handle}` at all. A pro past their 30-day chart window looking at a public client gets `canViewClient: false` and a handle — which is exactly the case that used to render a dead name (web) and "viewable on the web for now" (iOS).

null means "no public page exists" — render plain text, never a link.

clientConfirmation.description: Client-confirmation state (K11), derived by lib/booking/clientConfirmation.ts. OPTIONAL and absent when confirmation was never requested — every row until K12 ships the writers — so today's payload is byte-identical to pre-K11 and an old fixture still validates.

paymentBadge.description: At-a-glance payment state (deposit / paid / disputed …), computed by THE one helper (lib/booking/paymentBadge.ts) — iOS renders `label`/`tone` verbatim, never recomputing them on device (K1/K2).

relationshipBadge.description: NR/NNR/RR/RNR client-relationship mark (K5), mapped from the per-booking SNAPSHOT column by lib/booking/relationshipLabel.ts — iOS renders `label`/`description` verbatim (K6). `significant: false` (UNKNOWN) rows render no chip anywhere.

prepayScope.description: K10-B: per-service prepay requirement — sizes the pro-created deposit step.

cancelled.description: Rows this call transitioned to CANCELLED.

untouched.description: Rows it deliberately did NOT touch, each with the reason. Reported on the SUCCESS body for the same reason `skipped` is on the create body: a caller that renders only `cancelled` tells the pro the series is gone when part of it is still standing.

ProBookingSeriesCancelScope.description: Cancel scope. "This one" is deliberately ABSENT: it is the ordinary per-booking cancel (`PATCH /api/v1/pro/bookings/{id}`) and routing it through a series-shaped endpoint would fork one behaviour into two implementations.

depositHeldCents.description: Deposit money held against it. Cancelling does NOT refund it.

deferred.description: Set when creation stopped before the requested run was exhausted. Null means it attempted everything this pass was asked to attempt. The remaining dates are neither booked nor lost — the roll-forward adds them as they come into range.

nextOccurrenceIndex.description: Where K20's roll-forward resumes. Also the honest count of occurrences ATTEMPTED so far: occurrences.length + skipped.length.

timeZone.description: The zone the pattern steps through — the LOCATION's, not the viewer's. "Every Friday 9am" is 9am there, so every date above must be rendered in this zone or the pro reads a different day near midnight.

ProBookingSeriesDeferralDTO.description:
K20 — why creation stopped SHORT of the requested run, when it did.

🔴 Not a skip. A skip is permanent (`BookingSeriesException` is unique per index, so the roll-forward never retries it); this is a "not yet" that leaves no row behind and WILL be retried — today, a date past the pro's own booking horizon. Before K20 those became permanent `REFUSED` exceptions, which quietly made every series longer than the pro's booking window permanently short.

code.description: `BEYOND_WINDOW`, or the BookingErrorCode that deferred it. Diagnostic.

index.description: The first index this pass did not attempt.

intendedStart.description: The instant it would have taken, ISO-8601.

clientPublicProfileHandle.description:
The client's public `@handle`, or null when they have no public profile.

A SEPARATE axis from chart access: it says only whether a world-readable `/u/{handle}` page exists. null → render the name as plain text.

occurrenceCount.description: Planned total, or null for an open-ended series.

skipped.description: The durable skips — `BookingSeriesException` rows, oldest index first.

timeZone.description: The zone the pattern steps through — the LOCATION's.

ProBookingSeriesOccurrenceDTO.description: One appointment the materializer actually created.

index.description: 0-based and stable. Index 0 is the slot the pro picked.

scheduledFor.description: UTC instant, ISO-8601. Render it in `timeZone`.

bookedTotalCents.description: The service subtotal this occurrence was actually booked at, in cents — `Booking.subtotalSnapshot`. Occurrence 0's value is the series' PINNED price; a later occurrence that disagrees is price drift the pro is owed a sight of, not a rounding detail.

cancellable.description: True when a scoped cancel would transition this row. False rows carry `untouchedReason`.

depositHeldCents.description: Deposit money actually still held for this occurrence, in cents (`deriveNetDepositHeldCents` — net of refunds, zero while disputed). NOT a bill: a future occurrence has no final total yet. It is here because a scoped cancel does not refund, so the pro must see what they are holding before they cancel it away.

scheduledFor.description: UTC instant, ISO-8601. Render it in the series `timeZone`.

ProBookingSeriesPricingDTO.description: Price pinning (plan §Phase 8): the series is priced by what occurrence 0 was booked at, and drift is SURFACED rather than silently applied.

currentListTotalCents.description: The pro's CURRENT list price for this offering in this location mode plus the series' add-ons, in cents. Deliberately the catalog figure and labelled as such: what a given client is actually charged can differ (a price-grace ramp), so this is a comparison the pro can act on, never a prediction of the client's next bill.

listPriceMoved.description:
True when `currentListTotalCents` differs from `pinnedTotalCents`.

🔴 K20 settled what this MEANS, and it is not "your next occurrence will cost this": the roll-forward books every later occurrence at `pinnedTotalCents`, so a moved list price is information about the gap, and the pro's remedy is to end the series and start a new one. See lib/booking/series/pinnedPrice.ts. Any surface rendering this must say which of the two numbers the client will actually be charged.

occurrencesDisagree.description: True when a materialized occurrence disagrees with the pin.

pinnedTotalCents.description: Occurrence 0's booked service subtotal, in cents. The pin.

ProBookingSeriesRollForwardDTO.description:
K20 — whether this series still grows, and how far ahead.

A standing appointment that stops producing dates is the failure K18-B named and K19 refused to sell. This is the honest statement of the opposite: the dates the pro has NOT been shown yet, and the fact that something will create them.

leadDays.description: How far ahead of today the roll-forward keeps a series booked, in days.

pendingCount.description: Planned occurrences not yet attempted, or null for an open-ended series (which has no total to count down from).

willContinue.description:
True when the roll-forward will add more dates to this series.

🔴 False whenever the roll-forward cannot actually run — an ENDED or CANCELLED series, a plan with nothing left, and (the one that is easy to miss) the recurring-appointments feature being switched off. A surface that promised "new dates are added automatically" while the operator was dark would be the exact defect K19 refused to ship ([[verifiable-rail-still-needs-an-operator]]).

ProBookingSeriesSkippedOccurrenceDTO.description: One occurrence the materializer did NOT create, and why.

detail.description: The BookingErrorCode that refused it, or the impossible wall-clock time. Diagnostic, not user copy.

intendedStart.description: The instant the occurrence wanted, ISO-8601 — or null for NONEXISTENT_LOCAL_TIME, where no such instant exists (a DST gap). `detail` then carries the wall clock that does not exist.

ProBookingSeriesUntouchedReason.description: Why a scoped cancel left an occurrence alone. The list is the point: "cancel all" cannot mean the same thing for a visit that already happened as for an untouched future one, so every untouched row says which it was.

ProBusyDayDTO.description: One calendar day's commitments in the requested timezone.

blocked.description: Whether a calendar block touches that local day.

bookings.description: Occupying bookings (BOOKING_BLOCKING_STATUSES) starting that local day.

openSlots.description:
Bookable START TIMES left on that local day for the service the request named — "can I still fit someone in", as opposed to the two fields above, which only say how full the day already is (R4).

Present ONLY when `openSlots.computed` is true on the envelope, and then on EVERY day in range including zeroes — a fully-booked day and a day the server never counted must not look alike. Read the envelope first; don't infer "unknown" from a missing key here.

clientConfirmation.description:
Client-confirmation state (K11) — whether the CLIENT said they're coming, derived by the one helper (lib/booking/clientConfirmation.ts) from the loop's timestamp columns. Rendered as the card's CORNER GLYPH (K7's channel budget), with `description` in the accessible name.

OPTIONAL, and absent when confirmation was never requested — which, until K12 ships the writers, is every booking, so today's payload is byte-identical to pre-K11. Absent must always read as "not requested", never as an error. 🔴 NOT derived from BookingStatus: PENDING tracks the PRO's acceptance, the opposite direction.

clientProfileId.description: ClientProfile id, present only when this pro is allowed to open the client's chart (see getVisibleClientIdSetForPro). null keeps the id from leaking so the name renders as plain text for anyone without access.

clientPublicProfileHandle.description:
The client's public `@handle`, or null when they have no public profile.

A SEPARATE axis from `clientProfileId`: that one says "may this pro open the private chart", this one says "does a world-readable /u/{handle} page exist". A client outside the pro's 30-day chart window gets `clientProfileId: null` and a handle — the exact case whose name used to be dead text.

null means no public page exists: render plain text, never a link.

consentRequirement.description:
Unsigned-consent mark (K15) — the client owes a signature on a form the pro requires for one of this booking's services. Derived by the one helper (lib/consentForms/requirement.ts) and rendered as a TEXT CHIP ("Form due", warn tone) per K7's channel budget: NOT a colour, and NOT a second warning glyph, because the conflict triangle already owns that shape.

OPTIONAL, and absent unless there is genuinely an unsigned form on an appointment that has not happened yet — `significant` is false once the appointment is over, so a pro setting their first requirement does not light up their whole history in amber. It WARNS, never blocks.

🔴 This field shipped in K15 without being declared here, so it crossed to the device with zero contract coverage — the K4-B/K5-B gap reopened. It was invisible because the route adds it with a conditional SPREAD (`...(badge ? { consentRequirement: badge } : {})`), and TypeScript does not run excess-property checks on spread members. So this file's own header claim — "a field added to one and not the other is a compile error" — holds only for fields written as plain properties. Any future optional field must be declared HERE first, or `gen:api-schema` never sees it.

paymentBadge.description: At-a-glance payment state (deposit / paid / disputed …), derived by THE one helper (lib/booking/paymentBadge.ts) so this card, the bookings list and iOS can never disagree about what the money is doing (K1).

recurring.description:
Recurring-appointment mark (K19-C, shipped in K20) — this booking is one occurrence of a `BookingSeries`. Derived by the one helper (lib/booking/recurringMark.ts) and rendered in the card's TIME ROW beside the location chip, NOT as a sixth top-row chip and NOT as a second corner glyph: see that file for the channel call and why the crowded row was the wrong place for the least urgent fact on the card.

OPTIONAL, and absent on every booking that is not part of a series — which is all of them while `ENABLE_RECURRING_APPOINTMENTS` is unset, so today's payload is byte-identical to pre-K20.

🔴 Declared HERE **first**, before the route ever set it — which is the actual fix for the K15 gap above. The route adds it with the same conditional spread every other optional field uses (that is what keeps an absent mark byte-identical on the wire), and a spread is invisible to excess-property checking; so the declaration in this file, not the route, is what makes `gen:api-schema` and the iOS contract job see the field.

relationshipBadge.description: NR/NNR/RR/RNR client-relationship mark (K5) — mapped from the SNAPSHOT column by the one helper (lib/booking/relationshipLabel.ts); never derived from live history. iOS renders label/description verbatim (K6).

serviceSwatch.description:
The pro's colour for this booking's service (K7), resolved by the one helper (lib/calendar/eventColor.ts) and painted on the card's 4px accent stripe — the SERVICE channel, while status keeps the fill (decision D2).

OPTIONAL, and absent on every booking today: the swatch a pro picks is stored on `ProfessionalServiceOffering` by K8, so until then nothing has a colour of its own and the stripe keeps its status tone. Absent must always mean neutral, never a default hue — a colour nobody chose is a lie about which service this is.

ProCalendarHoldEventDTO.description:
A client's LIVE checkout reservation, shown so the pro's day tells the truth about what their time is doing. Before B5 the feed rendered BOOKING + BLOCK only, so a hold was invisible on the calendar AND in both overlap-warning surfaces that read this array — while the write path happily authorized a pro booking straight over it. [[reserving-a-slot-needs-a-surface]]

Deliberately ANONYMOUS (Tori's call, 2026-07-25): no clientName, no clientProfileId, no service name. A hold means somebody is mid-checkout this minute; the pro needs to know the slot is spoken for, not who is hesitating over it. It carries no `blockId`/`waitlistEntryId` because nothing acts on it — it is a read-only occupancy segment that expires on its own.

type.description: The PRO location's kind (SALON / SUITE / MOBILE_BASE …) — a `ProfessionalLocationType`, NOT the `ServiceLocationType` an event's `locationType` carries. The two enums are neighbours and don't overlap fully; `SUITE` exists only here.

professionalId.description: The authed pro's own id — used by the waitlist "Offer a time" modal to query availability (GET /api/v1/availability/day) for a proposed slot.

ProCalendarScopeDTO.description:
Which locations the events came from (K3). `LOCATION` means `location` is also the filter; `ALL` means it is ONLY the viewport anchor and the feed spans every location.

🔴 A client that adopts `location.id` as its own selection must gate that on this field, or asking for ALL bounces straight back to one location ([[two-states-owning-one-selection]]). An ABSENT `scope` (a pre-K3 server) must be read as LOCATION — that server always filtered, and reading its answer as "everything" is the original bug inverted.

ProCalendarWaitlistEventDTO.description: Synthetic BOOKING-kind event used only for the management.waitlistToday list. Waitlist entries are not real calendar occupancy, so this carries no location and a 'WAITLIST' status (part of the client BookingCalendarStatus union). It never enters the top-level `events` grid — only the management modal / stats tile.

clientPublicProfileHandle.description:
The client's public `@handle`, or null when they have no public profile.

A SEPARATE axis from `clientProfileId`: that one says "may this pro open the private chart", this one says "does a world-readable /u/{handle} page exist". A client outside the pro's 30-day chart window gets `clientProfileId: null` and a handle — the exact case whose name used to be dead text.

null means no public page exists: render plain text, never a link.

offerHref.description: Deep-link into the pre-filled new-booking flow (client + offering) so the pro can offer a matching slot. null when the pro has no active offering for the requested service.

pendingOffer.description: A still-PENDING offer already sent for this entry, so the row can show "Offer pending · <time>" instead of the offer action. null when none outstanding.

preferenceLabel.description: Human label for the client's preferred time (e.g. "Any time", "Morning", "Jun 14") shown in place of a concrete time on waitlist rows.

waitlistEntryId.description: The underlying waitlist entry + service/offering, so the pro can open the availability-aware "Offer a time" modal and POST a proposed slot. (id here is the raw WaitlistEntry.id — the row's `id` field carries the "waitlist:" prefix.)

bonus.description: Admin-granted bonus images for this month.

used.description: Images analyzed this month (0 while metering is off — nothing is counted).

ProCapabilitiesDTO.description:
Deployment-level switches for pro features that are built but held.

Each key is a capability the client may *offer*, not a per-pro entitlement: `true` means the endpoints behind it answer instead of 404ing. A client that cannot read this (offline, error) must treat every capability as `false` — hiding a live feature is recoverable, offering a dead one is not.

importFromAnotherApp.description: `ENABLE_PRO_MIGRATION` — the guided import wizard (services, clients, calendar) for a pro coming from another booking app.

noShowFees.description: `ENABLE_NO_SHOW_PROTECTION` — the pro's no-show / late-cancel fee policy settings, the client card-on-file rail, and real fee charging.

ProClientConsentRecordDTO.description:
A consent / patch-test record, ALREADY REDACTED by scope.

`scope` is the redaction that produced this row, not a display hint: `'full'` means the reading pro authored it and gets the proof fields, the notes and the form text; `'safety'` means it is another pro's patch test, reaching this pro only so they don't skin-test over someone else's result — result and validity travel, everything else is already null and `byName` names the other pro.

byName.description: Safety scope only — the pro whose record this is.

formVersion.description: K14 — null on every pre-K14 record, on any record whose pro attached no form, and on every safety-scoped row.

ProClientFormulaEntryDTO.description: A formula entry, author-scoped — free text is decrypted for its author only.

timeZone.description: IANA zone of that booking's location — render `when` in it, never the device's.

when.description: ISO instant of the booking this was recorded against, else its createdAt.

ProClientPolicyDTO.description: The four switches, exactly as stored. `null` for the whole object means the pro has set no policy for this client — which is a different fact from four falses, and the write route preserves the difference by DELETING the row rather than storing an all-false one.

blockSelfServeBooking.description: Client may not create a NEW appointment themselves.

prepayScope.description: Per-client prepay requirement, unioned with the offering's (wider wins).

requireCardOnFile.description: Client must have a saved card before a booking can be finalized.

requireDeposit.description: Widen the pro's deposit scope to cover this client's bookings.

cardOnFileRailEnabled.description:
Whether the save-card rail is live (ENABLE_NO_SHOW_PROTECTION).

A capability, not a policy value: while this is false the write route 409s a card-on-file requirement, so a client that renders that switch as available is offering something the server will refuse. The device must gate the CONTROL on this, not just handle the error ([[kill-switch-must-reach-the-control]]).

policy.description: The stored policy, or null when this pro has set nothing for this client.

ProConsentFormOptionDTO.description: K14 — one of the pro's ACTIVE consent forms, resolved to the version that would be signed today. This list is what lets a native record-entry surface offer the same choices web does; a picker that exists on one platform only is how a record ends up form-less on the other.

ProConsentFormVersionDTO.description: K14 — the exact form text a consent record attests to, resolved as it was signed. Author scope only: it travels with the proof fields, so a patch test's safety fields reaching another pro never carries the waiver text with them.

canExportTaxDocs.description: False when membership enforcement is on and the pro's plan lacks tax_export.

mileageRateCents.description: Current IRS standard mileage rate in cents/mile (e.g. 72.5) — lets the add-expense form preview a trip's deduction live.

receiptInbox.description: Captured receipts awaiting review (all-time PENDING, newest first).

receiptInboxAddress.description: The pro's forwarding address (<handle>@tovis.me) — premium only, else null.

mileageMiles.description: Logged business miles for a MILEAGE expense; null otherwise.

isAddressPublic.description: W7: the pro published this address to the public discovery surfaces.

ProNoShowSettingsDTO.description: A pro's account-level no-show / late-cancel fee policy.

cancelWindowHours.description: Hours before start inside which a client cancel is a billable late cancel.

chargeLateCancel.description: Charge when a client cancels inside the window.

chargeNoShow.description: Charge when the pro marks a booking as a no-show.

enabled.description: Master opt-in. While false the pro never charges a fee.

feeFlatAmount.description: Flat fee as a 2dp money string (e.g. "25.00"), or null when unset.

feePercent.description: Percent of the booking total (1–100), or null when unset.

feeType.description: How the fee is computed: a flat dollar amount or a percent of the total.

ProOpenSlotContextDTO.description:
Describes the open-slot overlay: whether it was computed, for what, and why not when it wasn't.

Always present on the envelope so a consumer can distinguish the three states explicitly instead of guessing from an absent field ([[optional-field-hides-a-required-one]]).

computed.description: True when every day in [from, to] carries an `openSlots` count.

durationMinutes.description: The appointment width the counts were computed for. A reschedule is sized from the BOOKING, everything else from the offering plus its add-ons, so this is echoed rather than assumed. Null when nothing was computed.

reason.description: Why counts are missing, when `computed` is false — a booking error code (e.g. "WORKING_HOURS_REQUIRED") or "SERVICE_NOT_FOUND". Null on success. For display, treat it as a reason to hide the overlay, not to fail: the day picker still works without counts.

dateHint.description: "YYYY-MM-DD" hint to prefill the confirm form (parsed date, pro's tz).

title.description: A human title: parsed vendor, else email subject, else a generic label.

enabled.description: Master opt-in. While false, no reminders are scheduled for this pro.

leads.description: The same offsets, humanized + structured for display/editing (longest first).

offsetMinutes.description: Lead-time offsets that fire a reminder, in minutes (sorted desc, deduped).

presets.description: Suggested lead-time presets the UI can offer as quick-adds.

ProReviewReplyDTO.description: The pro's public response to a review, as rendered on review surfaces.

repliedAtISO.description: When the reply was last written/edited (ISO-8601).

state.description: The hashable snapshot — unchanged by K17-A.

unsignedConsentForms.description:
Forms outstanding for THIS booking, omitted entirely when there are none or when the technical-record gate is off — so a pro who has bound no form gets a payload byte-identical to pre-K17-A.

Declared HERE rather than added at the route, because a field the route adds with a conditional spread never reaches `gen:api-schema` and crosses to the device with zero contract coverage — which is exactly how K15's calendar mark shipped uncovered (#812's first finding).

ProSessionUnsignedConsentFormDTO.description: One consent form this appointment needs and this client has not signed.

ProStrandedBookingDTO.description:
One booking that no longer fits the hours the pro just saved.

Reported, never acted on: B8's ruling (Tori, 2026-07-25) is warn-and-list — the save always succeeds and the bookings are left exactly as they are.

scheduledFor.description: ISO-8601 UTC instant. Render it in `timeZone`.

timeZone.description: IANA zone of that booking's location, for rendering `scheduledFor`.

ProStrandedBookingsDTO.description:
The bookings the just-saved hours strand.

`total` counts them all; `items` is capped (soonest first). The whole field is OMITTED when the save changed no hours, and is `null` when the scan itself failed — a warning we could not compute must not read as "nothing is wrong".

ProVisibilityActionDTO.description: Where the pro goes to pull this lever.

discoverable.description: False = the pro is filtered out of discovery entirely; levers are moot.

levers.description: Biggest lever first (ACTION → ATTENTION → GOOD → UNKNOWN, stable).

notMeasured.description: Inputs a pro might expect to matter that discovery does NOT read today. Stated plainly so the dashboard never implies coverage it doesn't have.

status.description: Worst lever status — drives the section header tone.

detail.description: Plain-language "here's how this affects discovery" — no weights.

headline.description: One-line verdict, written to be readable on its own.

ProVisibilityLookCountsDTO.description: Counts behind the LOOK_COVERAGE lever, shown as a breakdown strip.

distinctServiceCount.description: Distinct services represented across feed-eligible looks. Services, not categories: groupBy can't traverse Service → ServiceCategory, and "you have looks for 3 of your services" is the more concrete read for a pro anyway. Display only — the coverage lever's status keys off looks + tags.

distinctTagCount.description: Distinct non-banned tags across feed-eligible looks (match surface).

feedEligibleCount.description: Pro-authored looks that clear every gate the pro controls.

pendingReviewCount.description: Published but still awaiting moderation — nothing for the pro to do.

ProVisibilityStatus.description: ACTION  — discovery is actively held back and the pro can fix it now. ATTENTION — a real lift is being left on the table. GOOD    — this input is healthy. UNKNOWN — not measured yet (cron hasn't populated, or too little data to           judge). Never the pro's fault; carries no blame copy.

missingLocation.description: True when no bookable location of that mode exists yet.

usedDefault.description: True when the pro has never saved hours and these are the defaults.

strandedBookings.description: Absent when the hours did not change; null when the scan failed.

updatedCount.description: How many locations this save wrote to.

ownerProfilePublic.description: Whether the owner's /u/[handle] profile is itself public (back-link gate).

followingOwner.description: The signed-in client follows the board owner.

isOwn.description: The signed-in client is looking at their OWN board.

following.description: The signed-in client already follows this profile.

isOwn.description: The signed-in client is looking at their OWN profile.

serviceNames.description: Display names for `serviceIds`, in the same tag order. Native clients render these as the tile's service chips (web's `/media/[id]` resolves the same names server-side); empty when the media carries no service tags.

before.description: Paired "before" for the comparison slider, or null when not paired.

RecurringMark.description: The recurring mark for one booking. Absent (null) for every booking that is not part of a series, which is all of them until a pro creates one.

description.description: Plain words for the accessible name and the iOS label. The mark itself is a shape; screen readers do not get shapes (K5's rule), and iOS renders this verbatim rather than rebuilding the sentence (K6's rule).

occurrenceNumber.description: 1-based for humans. `Booking.seriesOccurrenceIndex` is 0-based and stays that way everywhere it is a KEY (the unique constraint, the cancel scope, the exception rows); this is the only place it becomes an ordinal, because "appointment 0 of 12" is not a thing anyone says.

description.description: Plain-words expansion ("New client · requested you") for tooltips and accessibility labels — the marks are shorthand and screen readers should not spell out bare letters.

label.description: The salon-book mark itself ("NR") — what the chip prints.

significant.description: false only for UNKNOWN: an unclassified row renders NO chip anywhere — absence is the honest display for "nobody recorded this", and a wall of "Unknown" on imported history is noise. The DECISION lives here so surfaces can't drift on it.

ReminderLeadDTO.description: A single configured reminder lead time, both as the scalar SSOT (minutes) and humanized/structured for display + editing.

label.description: Human label, e.g. "1 week before", "4 hours before".

minutes.description: Minutes before the appointment this reminder fires. The scalar SSOT.

unit.description: Whether {value} counts days or hours before the appointment.

value.description: The lead time as a whole number of {unit}, for the value + unit editor.

ReminderLeadInputDTO.description: A single reminder lead time as submitted by the editor.

value.description: A whole number of {unit} before the appointment.

ReminderLeadUnit.description: The unit a reminder lead time is expressed in when editing.

ReminderPresetDTO.description: A suggested lead-time preset offered as a quick-add in the editor.

unit.description: Whether {value} counts days or hours before the appointment.

value.description: The lead time as a whole number of {unit}.

thread.description:
The resolved (or just-created) thread, as the same row the inbox list returns — null when nothing resolved and `createIfMissing` was false.

The full row is carried, not just the id, so a caller can open the thread from one round trip. A brand-new thread has no messages and the inbox deliberately hides message-less threads, so "resolve, then find it in the list" could never work for the FIRST message to a client. Additive: earlier clients that read only `thread.id` are unaffected.

isAddressPublic.description:
W7: true when `formattedAddress`/`placeId`/coordinates on THIS preview are the pro's real ones because they chose to publish them. False means the preview is redacted — address null, coordinates coarsened to a ~1.1km grid.

Consumers must branch on this rather than on "is lat/lng present": a coarsened coordinate is still a coordinate, which is exactly how Discover came to render a Navigate button over a fuzzed point.

locationType.description: W7: SALON / SUITE / MOBILE_BASE. A mobile base is never a destination.

unsignedConsentForms.description:
K17-web — consent forms this client still owes for this appointment (K15). Web's session page renders the same list as `UnsignedConsentBanner`; this is how the native session hub gets it.

OPTIONAL and ABSENT when there is nothing outstanding, so a pro who has bound no form sees a payload byte-identical to pre-K17. Absent means "nothing to sign", never an error — and it WARNS, never blocks.

🔴 Not the calendar's `significant`-gated badge: at session start the appointment time has arrived, which is exactly when that gate would suppress the warning. See the note above `loadUnsignedConsentFormsForBookings`.

UnsignedConsentForm.description: One unsigned form, in the words a session-start surface prints.

kindLabel.description: `kind` as words, from the one label table (K14).

lastSeenAt.description: Most recent push-token activity for this device (ISO), or null.

pushActive.description: At least one push token for this device is still active.

revoked.description: This device's session has been revoked.

revokedAt.description: When the device session was revoked (ISO), or null.
